deep_analysis.executive_intro:
The FTSE screen is broadly neutral: 140 holds dominate versus 68 combined buys (19 strong buys, 49 buys) and 41 avoids, so value signals are selective rather than market-wide. All five top candidates carry a strong-buy label and pass all five model families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk), but Industrials appear twice (FirstGroup, ME Group) alongside one Healthcare, one Communication Services, and one Agriculture/Commodities name—suggesting cyclical and income-oriented clusters rather than a single-sector theme. Conviction is uniformly modest (50–56%) and every name is new to the signal (one week), with neutral timing across the board. A key caution: several names show material gaps between filing-aligned FCF and screen TTM figures (HIK.L, MEGP.L, ITV.L), NCAV is unavailable for all top picks, and MEGP.L was adjusted from strong buy to buy on an interim-quality overlay—figures should be verified against primary filings before sizing positions.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Eleven of 22 models passed (composite 92%, sector-relative 86%), led by Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (37.3%), Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality, with key metrics P/E 9.2, P/B 1.4, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.7%. Failures cluster on balance-sheet quality: Financial Health (D/E 161%, current ratio 0.73), Graham Enterprising (excessive leverage, earnings growth −5.9%), Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat. documents.name: FirstGroup plc
documents.executive_summary: FirstGroup plc is a UK-focused public transport operator (First Bus and First Rail) that has completed a multi-year pivot away from North American assets and is now delivering sustained adjusted earnings growth, strong cash conversion, and active capital returns. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy on cheapness (P/E ~9.2, earnings yield ~10.9%), exceptional filing-aligned free cash flow (FCF yield ~37%), dividend growth, and a Piotroski F-Score of 8/9, with 11 of 22 models passing across five factor families. The valuation hook is a de-rated, cash-generative UK transport franchise trading below typical quality multiples despite adjusted EPS rising from 11.6p (FY 2024) to 19.4p (FY 2025) and management guiding to modest FY 2026 growth. The central debate is whether earnings diversification (London bus, open-access rail, Rail Services, London Overground) offsets structural headwinds from bus franchising policy, fare-cap transitions, employers’ National Insurance, and the phased transfer of DfT National Rail Contracts to public ownership—issues that screens only partially capture through leverage and liquidity flags.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, FirstGroup offers a rare combination of low headline valuation, improving adjusted profitability, and disciplined capital allocation after a successful portfolio simplification. The screen’s strong-buy signal (composite score 92%, sector-relative 86%) is anchored in metrics that map to real filing trends: adjusted revenue rose from £1,279.6m (FY 2024) to £1,370.0m (FY 2025), adjusted operating profit from £204.3m to £222.8m, and adjusted EPS from 16.7p to 19.4p, with free cash flow before acquisitions and returns more than doubling to £113.5m (FY 2025 presentation). Management returned c.£126m via dividends and buybacks in FY 2025 and launched further repurchase programmes; H1 2026 adjusted EPS of 9.9p (+16% YoY) and an interim dividend of 2.2p support the dividend and GARP model passes.

Business quality is stronger than the “cyclical bus operator” label implies. First Bus is scaling in London (RATP London acquisition), electrifying fleet and depots (c.1,280 zero-emission buses at H1 2026), and building B2B/coach revenues. First Rail combines fee-based DfT TOC exposure (declining but with anticipated c.£125m cash inflow over three years from contract transitions) with higher-quality open-access and Rail Services earnings; the London Overground preferred-operator award (~£3bn over eight years, revenue risk retained by TfL) adds further diversification. The Piotroski score (8/9) and passes on earnings quality, acquirer’s multiple, and composite value corroborate operational improvement, even as Graham-, Buffett-, and moat-style models fail on leverage (debt/equity ~161%), weak liquidity (current ratio ~0.73), and ROE (16.7%) below stricter quality thresholds. The screen’s strong-buy case is therefore best read as “mispriced cash and earnings power in transition,” not pristine balance-sheet quality.
documents.financial_review:
Primary sources: IR presentations (`ir_5ba5b17047f87036.txt`, `ir_af873270e9c4b29f.txt`), H1 2026 press release (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`), Companies House annual bodies (`ch_SC157176_MzQ3MzQwMTk5MmFkaXF6a2N4.txt` et al.). `filings_index.json` confirms all 11 bodies present (`with_body: 11`; refetched 2026-08-09). The new fetch (`d2cdf72fa5d7df13.txt`) is Investegate market commentary—not used for figures below.

**Adjusted earnings (filings — preferred)**

| Period | Adj. revenue | Adj. OP | Adj. EPS | Adj. FCF (pre-acq/returns) | Adj. net debt |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------|---------------------------|---------------|
| FY 2024 | £1,279.6m | £204.3m | 16.7p | £53.9m | £64.1m net cash |
| FY 2025 | £1,370.0m | £222.8m | 19.4p | £113.5m | £86.9m |
| H1 2026 | £833.6m | £103.6m | 9.9p | £(35.6)m | £207.6m |

Management guides modest FY 2026 adjusted EPS growth and year-end adjusted net debt £125m–£135m (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`).

**Statutory vs screen earnings (Yahoo — secondary)**

Yahoo statutory net income $127.5m→$118.3m drives the −5.9% screen input and Graham/Lynch failures. This diverges from filing-adjusted EPS because rail IFRS 16 consolidation, historical pension settlements (FY 2024 LGPS charge £146.9m in `ch_SC157176_MzQzMTExOTQ4OGFkaXF6a2N4.txt`), and buyback-driven per-share effects sit on different bases.

**Free cash flow — methodology gap**

| Metric | FY 2025 | H1 2026 |
|--------|---------|---------|
| Screen/Yahoo FCF | ~$362.6m canonical (FY 2026 USD) | — |
| Company adjusted FCF | £113.5m | £(35.6)m |

FY 2025 bridge (`ir_5ba5b17047f87036.txt`): adjusted EBITDA £163.4m → cash from operations £207.4m → adjusted FCF £113.5m; IFRS 16 leasing strip £248.6m explains most of the gap to statutory flows. H1 2026 outflow reflects accelerated First Bus electrification (net capex c.£105m; FY 2026 guide c.£180m). **The 37.3% screen FCF yield is not normalized owner earnings.**

**Margins**

Group adjusted operating margin 16.3% at FY 2025 compressed to 12.4% H1 2026; First Bus 6.1% (−190 bps) on fare-cap transition, −4% underlying volumes, and NIC headwinds—substantiating Quality Value and Buffett Quality failures.

**Balance sheet and pension**

- **Adjusted net debt:** £207.6m at H1 2026 (cash £188.2m less bank borrowings/overdrafts/finance leases/NextGen battery debt £23.6m); excludes ring-fenced TOC cash (£232.8m) and IFRS 16 rail leases (`ir_af873270e9c4b29f.txt`).
- **Reported net debt:** £992.0m including £1,017.2m IFRS 16 leases.
- **Pension:** Bus triennial 2024 complete; £20m returned; c.£65m escrow; RPS shared-cost for rail (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`). IAS 19 funded-status not in pack.

**Remaining gaps:** Full statutory income statement, complete H1 2026 adjusting-items note (body truncates at `ir_032b08900a650e14.txt` line 844), pension IAS 19 and covenant detail from Companies House PDF.

documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced (filings)**

- **Bus margins and volumes:** First Bus margin 6.1% H1 2026; underlying volumes −4%; £3 fare cap and c.£16m NIC impact (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`).
- **Rail transition:** SWR transferred May 2025; further NRC transfers scheduled; c.£125m cash inflow over three years partially offsets declining TOC fees; London Overground preferred-operator award (~£3bn, TfL retains revenue risk; `aefbcf7637993f73.txt`).
- **Capex cycle:** H1 adjusted FCF outflow £(35.6)m; adjusted net debt rising £86.9m→£207.6m; FY 2026 net capex guide c.£180m.
- **Screen metric distortion:** High D/E and low current ratio reflect consolidated IFRS 16 balance sheet; quality-model failures are directionally valid even if headline leverage overstates economic risk.
- **Pension escrow:** c.£65m held pending 2030 valuations.

**Partially open**

- **Sustainable FCF yield:** Directionally resolved as methodology-inflated; normalised mid-cycle adjusted FCF after FY 2026 electrification peak unquantified.
- **Statutory earnings decline:** Basis mismatch with growing adjusted EPS; precise FY 2026 adjusting-items schedule incomplete in available bodies.
- **Covenant headroom:** Policy stated (<2.0×); numeric headroom requires borrowings note from Companies House PDF.

**Secondary context (new body)**

`d2cdf72fa5d7df13.txt` cites dividend rising “from 6.5p to 7.2p”—conflicts with filing-stated FY 2025 total dividend of 6.5p (`ir_5ba5b17047f87036.txt`). Treat 7.2p as unverified commentary.

PwC H1 2026 review (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`) found no material going-concern uncertainties identified by directors; this does not remove bus-policy, rail-transition, or capex-cycle risks.

documents.news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is moderate-to-heavy on capital returns and results, thinner on deep operational analysis. Material items from `news_manifest.json`:

- **H1 2026 results (18 November 2025):** “FirstGroup H1 2026: Earnings and Revenue Rise, Shares Tumble” (AskTraders) and “Why did this FTSE 250 growth star just plunge 14%?” (The Twelfth Magpie)—market reaction diverged from adjusted EPS growth to 9.9p.
- **FY 2025 / capital return (June 2025):** “FirstGroup launches £100 million share buyback to cut share capital” (The Globe and Mail); yfinance summary of FY 2026 earnings call citing 25% revenue increase and £100m buyback.
- **London Overground (9 December 2025):** “FirstGroup wins $4 billion London Overground rail contract, shares rise” (Reuters); RNS confirms preferred-operator status, ~£3bn/8-year contract from May 2026, TfL retains revenue risk.
- **AGM and ongoing buybacks (July–August 2026):** “FirstGroup Shareholders Back Board, Dividend and Capital Actions at 2026 AGM” (TipRanks); multiple “Transaction in Own Shares” and buyback progress updates.
- **Strategy context (May 2025):** “FirstGroup can grow despite rail nationalisation, says broker” (Proactive Investors).
- **Policy link (July 2025):** “3 UK Transport Stocks Linked To The £2 Bus Fare Cap” (simplywall.st)—relevant backdrop to bus volume pressure.

Promotional “40–55% upside” pieces from DirectorsTalk dominate lower-signal coverage; treat as sentiment, not fundamental evidence. No material M&A beyond bolt-on coach acquisitions and London Overground award surfaced in the manifest.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary:
Hikma is a diversified generic and branded pharmaceutical group (Injectables, Branded MENA, Hikma Rx) reporting in US dollars, with FY2025 core revenue of $3,349m (+6%) and core operating profit of $741m (+3%) per the 26 February 2026 full-year results release. The quantitative screen flags the stock as a strong buy on cheapness (P/E 12.8, P/B 1.9), quality (ROE 15.4%), dividend (3.8% yield), GARP, and balance-sheet metrics (D/E 77%), though FCF yield and earnings-quality screens fail. The valuation hook is a mid-teens earnings multiple on a globally diversified pharma platform that has compounded core earnings through 2022–2025, now paired with a $250m buyback and 5% dividend increase. The central debate is whether Injectables margin pressure, one-off legal cash outflows, and withdrawn medium-term guidance are temporary reset costs—or evidence that the recovery narrative (reinforced by a strong H1 2026 profit beat in press coverage) still lacks filing-verified runway.

---
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination of sector-defensive end-markets, geographic diversification (North America, MENA, Europe), and headline valuation that passes multiple classic screens simultaneously: Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Financial Health. At P/E 12.8 and P/B 1.9 with a 3.8% yield and ROE of 15.4%, the market prices in sustained Injectables disappointment rather than the Branded segment's double-digit growth (core revenue +10%, core operating profit +19% in FY2025) and Hikma Rx margin improvement.

Business quality is supported by filing evidence: S&P and Fitch upgraded the group to BBB in FY2025; net debt/core EBITDA was 1.6x at year-end ($1,387m net debt on $853m core EBITDA); return on average invested capital was 16.0%; and the board announced a $250m share buyback alongside an 84c total dividend (+5%). The Darwazah family's return to operational leadership (Said Darwazah as CEO from December 2025) and board refresh (Victoria Hull as Chair, Tobias Hestler appointed NED in August 2026 per news) signal a strategy reset focused on execution over medium-term targets.

The screen's strong-buy signal is directionally supported by fundamentals, but conviction is tempered: filing-aligned free cash flow was only $119m in FY2025 (OCF $436m less elevated capex/investment), down from $329m in 2024, and the screen itself notes weak TTM FCF ($14.4m) versus filing-aligned $119m—a data-quality flag rather than a rejection. Failed screens (FCF Yield, Earnings Quality, Economic Moat, Piotroski 6/9) correctly highlight that cheapness here comes with cyclical generic pricing pressure and lumpy cash conversion, not pure balance-sheet deep value.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates automated instant-service vending — chiefly photobooths (Photo.ME) and unattended laundry (Wash.ME) — across 16 countries, with laundry now the primary growth engine. The quantitative screen rates the name a **strong buy** (15/22 models; composite 82%; P/E 8.1×, yield 6.9%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%), but an interim-quality overlay already moderates the headline to **Buy** given H1 EPS decline and sub-1.0× FCF/dividend coverage. FY2025 (to 31 October 2025) delivered record profitability (£78.2m PBT, £115.5m cash from operations), yet H1 2026 showed softer April trading in France and revised full-year PBT guidance of **£69–74m** — a step down from FY2025. The investment case rests on a cash-generative, asset-light vending model trading at a deep earnings and dividend yield, with laundry rollout and an £18m buyback supporting returns; the key debate is whether near-term consumer/geopolitical headwinds and photobooth regulatory drag are cyclical, or mark a peak in the earnings cycle that the screen has not fully priced.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MEGP offers a rare combination of **cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk** passes (five of five model families). At ~8× trailing earnings and nearly 7% yield on filing-aligned cash flows, the market appears to discount a meaningful earnings reset already under way: management guides FY2026 PBT **£69–74m** versus **£78.2m** in FY2025, and H1 2026 diluted EPS fell **3.9%** to **6.48p** (from **6.74p**). The screen’s filing-aligned FCF of **£25.2m** (FY2025) versus TTM screen FCF of **£15.6m** highlights the tension — historical cash conversion is strong, but heavy growth capex (£65.6m FY2025; £33.9m in H1 2026 alone) compresses free cash available for dividends.

Business quality supports the value case. ME Group holds dominant photobooth positions and is scaling laundry rapidly: net laundry units rose **1,145** in FY2025 to **7,607**, with Wash.ME EBITDA of **£55.5m** approaching Photo.ME’s **£59.3m** (46% of group EBITDA). EBITDA margin improved to **38.2%** (from 37.1%). Net cash stood at **£26.5m** at October 2025 (gross cash **£56.5m**; lease-adjusted), and the board launched an **£18m share buyback** in March 2026 alongside a dividend policy targeting **>55%** of post-tax profits (FY2025 total dividend **8.64p**, up 9.5%).

The screen’s failures are informative rather than disqualifying: Graham Defensive (current ratio 1.54× vs 2.0× threshold), Piotroski F-Score **6/9**, and Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion) — all consistent with a capex-heavy growth phase and recent earnings softness. The adjusted **Buy** (from Strong Buy) on interim overlay aligns with this first-pass view: accumulate on valuation, but size for medium risk around France concentration, governance, and the FY2026 profit step-down.

rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=30%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 3 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Costs: 3.0% applied on each buy and sell.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.
plan.summary: Next rebalance would target 3 equal-weight sleeve(s); leave 2 near-target holding(s).
